desc:
Ecom Swift LLC provides Android app maintenance and updates in a fixed starter sprint: newer build tools, libraries and target API level, plus bug fixes and a tested release bundle, so your app stays current with Android and Google Play.

## What is Android app maintenance?

Android app maintenance is the regular work that keeps a shipped app compatible, stable and allowed in the store. It includes updating Android Studio and Gradle, upgrading libraries, raising the target API level, fixing crashes and warnings, and testing on current devices.

None of it adds a new feature. It protects the ones you already have.

## Why apps fall behind

Android changes every year, and Google Play changes its rules with it. Each new Android version can alter permissions, background work, notifications or storage access. Libraries release security fixes and drop support for old versions. Play asks developers to target a recent API level, and apps that do not may be hidden from new users or blocked from receiving updates.

An app left alone for a season or two can slowly turn into a risk. Crashes appear on new phones, a payment library stops working, and an update to fix one bug suddenly needs a dozen other changes at once. Small, regular maintenance is easier and cheaper than a late rescue.

## How maintenance affects stability and store standing

Users notice stability more than they notice code. Fewer crashes and freezes lead to better ratings and more users who stay. Android vitals in Play Console track crash and freeze rates, and poor numbers there can reduce how widely your app is shown. We cannot promise store ranking changes, but a healthy app removes known reasons for a penalty.

Maintenance also lowers future costs. Clean dependencies, fewer warnings and removed unused code make every later feature quicker to build and safer to ship.

## What a good maintenance sprint includes

- A build that opens and compiles on the latest stable Android Studio.
- Gradle, Kotlin and plugin versions brought up to date where safe.
- The target API level raised to what Google Play currently asks for.
- Outdated libraries replaced or upgraded, with notes on each change.
- Fixes for crashes, warnings and deprecated calls.
- A look at Android vitals: crash rate, freezes and startup behavior.
- Permissions and data safety answers checked against what the code actually does.
- Testing on several current Android versions and screen sizes.
- A release bundle ready to upload, signed through your own signing setup.
- A written report that explains every change and what remains.

## How we work

We start with a health check: can the project build, what is outdated, what do your Play Console numbers show. Then we agree the list of fixes and upgrades that fit the package. The Basic package covers the build check, the target API check, a few small fixes and a health report. Standard updates libraries, raises the target API, fixes more issues and delivers a tested bundle. Premium adds performance and memory checks, a permissions review and cleanup of unused code, then closes with a care plan.

Ongoing monthly care is quoted separately. The starter sprint stands on its own.

## Do and avoid for app upkeep

**Do:**
- Share your crash reports and Play Console warnings.
- Tell us which features must never break.
- Keep a record of the keys and signing details in your own safe place.
- Test the release bundle with a small group first.
- Plan a sprint at least once a year.

**Avoid:**
- Waiting until Play sends a final warning.
- Upgrading every library on the same day without tests.
- Ignoring deprecation messages in the build output.
- Keeping a library that nobody maintains without a plan to replace it.
- Adding new features in the same release as a major upgrade.

## Who this is for

An owner who received a policy email about the target API level and does not know where to begin. A company whose app works but whose original developer has gone. A team that has put out features for a year without touching dependencies. A founder who wants a clear health report before deciding whether to invest further.

## What we need from you

Send the repository, a short note on how the app is built and released, and access to read Android vitals. We ask to be added as a collaborator or limited user, never with your passwords. If an upload to Play is wanted, you can add us to your Play Console with release permission, or upload the bundle yourself.
